marker_reviews.reason: The EXECUTE format() on line 185 is a read-only existence probe inside the BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE guard core.require_direct_support_for_canonical_edge(). It runs only while a row is being written, it creates, alters and drops no catalog object, and it writes no row, so a post-apply catalog assertion has no durable target to bind to. Its identifiers are not user input: they are the three literal trigger arguments written in this same migration, passed through format %s and %I quoting, so no untrusted text can reach the statement. The behaviour it implements - that an inferred or co-occurrence support edge can never sustain a direct canonical bridge row - is asserted instead in supabase/tests/canonical_licensing_relationship_bridges.sql, which runs against an ephemeral database on every pull request.

The two EXECUTE format() statements on lines 258 and 270 are read-only existence probes inside the BEFORE UPDATE guard core.refuse_unsupporting_update_of_support_edge(), added to close review finding H-1. They run only while a support-edge row is being updated, they create, alter and drop no catalog object, and they write no row, so a post-apply catalog assertion has no durable target to bind to. Their identifiers are not user input: the bridge table and the two column names are the three literal trigger arguments written in this same migration, and the support-edge table name comes from tg_table_schema/tg_table_name, all passed through format %s and %I quoting, so no untrusted text can reach either statement. The behaviour they implement - that withdrawing the last current direct source assertion behind a standing canonical edge is refused, while supersession by replacement stays free - is asserted instead in supabase/tests/canonical_licensing_relationship_bridges.sql steps 5d and 5e, which run against an ephemeral database on every pull request.

The two EXECUTE format() statements on lines 350 and 363 are read-only existence probes inside the deferrable constraint trigger function core.assert_canonical_edge_still_supported(), added to close the round-2 review finding that a single bulk UPDATE statement slips past the BEFORE row guard because a row trigger cannot see its own statement's other-row effects. They run only at commit time while checking a support-edge row that was updated or deleted, they create, alter and drop no catalog object, and they write no row, so a post-apply catalog assertion has no durable target to bind to. Their identifiers are not user input: the bridge table and the two column names are the three literal trigger arguments written in this same migration, and the support-edge table name comes from tg_table_schema/tg_table_name, all passed through format %s and %I quoting, so no untrusted text can reach either statement. The behaviour they implement - that no statement shape may leave a canonical bridge row standing with no current direct source assertion under it - is asserted instead in supabase/tests/canonical_licensing_relationship_bridges.sql step 5f2, which runs against an ephemeral database on every pull request.

The EXECUTE format() on line 441 is a read-only single-column lookup inside the BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE guard core.require_support_edge_licensor_matches_endpoints(), added to close the round-3 review finding that a support row's licensor_id was NOT NULL and in the identity key yet tied to nothing, so a loader could file one licensor's endpoint pair under another licensor's id with no error. It runs only while a support-edge row is being written, it creates, alters and drops no catalog object, and it writes no row, so a post-apply catalog assertion has no durable target to bind to. Its identifier is not user input: the endpoint entity table name is one of the four literal trigger arguments written in this same migration, passed through format %s quoting, so no untrusted text can reach the statement. The function pins search_path to pg_catalog, pg_temp and revokes EXECUTE from public, anon and authenticated, so it is reachable only as a trigger. The behaviour it implements - that a claim's licensor must be the licensor its endpoints declare, whenever they declare one - is asserted instead in supabase/tests/canonical_licensing_relationship_bridges.sql step 6b, which runs against an ephemeral database on every pull request.
